message.content: I'll stay in jail and roll for doubles. Paying to leave just puts me on a board I can't survive.
message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to pay the $50 jail fine or roll for doubles.

I have $389 and no get-out-of-jail cards. p2 is dominant with $1698 and four houses on light blues. p1 is weak with only $147. I own Baltic and Virginia but no monopoly.

p2 also owns dark blues, railroads, and utilities. p4 is bankrupt. I have no get-out-of-jail card. I will roll for doubles to avoid the $50 fine.

Paying the $50 fine would leave me with $339. From jail, I would land on St. Charles ($10) and Electric Company ($12). I am calculating whether this is survivable against p2's monopolies.

I am mapping the spaces after jail. I would land on Virginia, two railroads, and New York. Most other properties are mortgaged or lack monopolies. I am checking whether Atlantic is unmortgaged.

Atlantic is unmortgaged but part of a mortgaged set, so it does not collect rent. Ventnor, Water Works, Marvin, and Pacific are all mortgaged. I would land on Go to Jail and then on North Carolina.

I am calculating exact rent costs from jail. Rolling a 7 would land me on Pennsylvania Ave ($28), Short Line ($200), and then Park Place ($1300) or Boardwalk ($1700). Both are instant death. Rolling a 6 would hit Virginia, the Penn RR, and St James. I am weighing whether to pay the $50 fine and leave immediately.

Paying the $50 fine would not immediately land me on dangerous spaces. I would still roll 2 through 12 and remain in the relatively safe zone of spaces 12 through 22, including New York at $16. The first turn out of jail is therefore equally safe whether I pay the fine or roll for doubles.

I will stay in jail as long as possible. I have no monopoly, so missing rent income is irrelevant. I have three chances to roll doubles before being forced to pay the fine. Even a doubles roll of 5+5 lands on Free Parking, which is safe.

I am now calculating exact rent values for light blue properties with four houses. Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut each cost $400. St. Charles and States cost $625. Virginia costs $700. These figures confirm that paying the $50 fine would expose me to severe rent pressure.

Do not pay $50. Next: keep rolling doubles until forced; never fund p2; don't sell Baltic/Virginia."}
